name: W205 C300 stock exhaust (approximate)
notes: First model of the reference car. Layout, lengths and muffler internals are placeholders from forum measurements and owner inspection; replace with caliper, tape and thermocouple readings. The underfloor element is unverified (cat or resonator): modelled as a resonator chamber. The rear muffler is modelled as one expansion chamber with two outlets; its real internals and the vacuum flap (if fitted) are unknown.

engine.valves.valves_per_cylinder.source: M274: four valves per cylinder, two exhaust

engine.geometry.rod_mm.source: from memory; Heywood (1988) §2.2 gives rod length over crank radius l/a = 3 to 4 for small and medium engines, which on a 46 mm crank radius is 138–184 mm

engine.valves.valve_diameter_mm.source: from memory; engineering reasoning: two exhaust valves beside two intake valves in an 83 mm bore leave exhaust heads of about 0.28–0.35 of the bore, 23–29 mm; replace with the head specification or a caliper reading

engine.valves.throat_diameter_mm.source: from memory; engineering reasoning: the inner seat diameter is the head less twice the seat face and margin (1.0–2.0 mm each side), 0.83–0.90 of a 26 mm head

engine.valves.discharge_coefficient.source: constant standing in for a lift-dependent curve; engineering reasoning: exhaust poppet-valve discharge coefficients referred to the smaller of curtain and throat area lie between about 0.55 and 0.75 over the lift event; replace with flow-bench data

engine.valves.evo_deg.source: placeholder; SI exhaust valves typically open 40–60° before BDC (Heywood 1988, ch. 6), 120–140° after firing TDC, widened by ±10° for the M274 exhaust cam phaser, whose authority is not published

engine.valves.evc_deg.source: placeholder; SI exhaust valves typically close 8–20° after TDC (Heywood 1988, ch. 6), 368–380° after firing TDC, widened by ±10° for the exhaust cam phaser

engine.valves.max_lift_mm.source: placeholder; the input specification's rule L/D = 0.25–0.30 on a 26 mm head gives 6.5–7.8 mm; the 8 mm in use came from memory, so the range is kept wide enough to hold it

engine.polytropic_exponent.source: engineering reasoning: burned gas at 1100–1500 K has γ ≈ 1.28–1.33 (the gas table); heat loss to the walls during blowdown lowers the exponent below γ

turbine.extraction_factor.source: placeholder; engineering reasoning: small automotive turbines reach total-to-static efficiencies of about 0.6–0.75 at their best points and less under pulsating flow and with the wastegate open

turbine.scrolls.manifold_volume_l.source: from memory; engineering reasoning: ports, runners and one scroll of a twin-scroll housing on a 2.0 L four, ±30 % until measured by water fill

turbine.scrolls.nozzle_area_cm2.source: placeholder; effective nozzle area with wastegate is not published for this turbocharger; a factor of 1.5 either way is an engineering judgment until a turbine map is supplied

turbine.scrolls.heat_loss_w_per_k.source: from memory; engineering reasoning: a coolant-jacketed integrated manifold, a factor of 2 either way

turbine.coolant_temperature_k.source: engineering reasoning: coolant after the thermostat, 85–100 °C in normal running

operating.map_kpa.source: from memory; engineering reasoning: road-load cruise of a 2.0 L turbocharged engine sits near 45–65 kPa manifold pressure

operating.intake_temperature_k.source: engineering reasoning: intercooled charge air at part load lies between ambient and about 40 K above it

operating.volumetric_efficiency.source: engineering reasoning: four-valve SI engines at mid speed breathe 0.8–0.95 of the manifold density (Heywood 1988, ch. 6)

operating.heat_retained.source: engineering reasoning: combustion efficiency 0.95–0.98 times one less the wall heat loss during combustion and expansion to EVO, 10–25 % of the fuel energy

operating.n_compression.source: engineering reasoning: polytropic compression of the fresh charge with wall heat transfer, 1.28–1.36

operating.n_expansion.source: engineering reasoning: polytropic expansion of burned gas from TDC to EVO, below γ ≈ 1.3 through heat loss, 1.25–1.33

operating.lhv_mj_per_kg.source: lower heating value of gasoline, 43 MJ/kg (Heywood 1988, Appendix D)

gas.lambda.source: engineering reasoning: a three-way-catalyst engine dithers about λ = 1 by about ±2 % at cruise; the model takes λ ≥ 1 (rich products are not modelled), so the lean half is swept

ambient.underbody_air_factor.source: engineering reasoning: air speed in the underbody gap as a fraction of vehicle speed, the pipes sitting in the underbody boundary layer

ambient.ground_z_mm.source: from memory; engineering reasoning: the downpipe flange sits 0.6–0.7 m above the road; measure with a tape

system.elements.cat.cpsi.source: substrate fallback of the input specification: 600 cpsi (400–900)

system.elements.cat.cell_wall_mm.source: substrate fallback of the input specification: 2–4 mil; 3 mil in use

system.elements.cat.source: can dimensions from memory; ±10 % until measured

system.elements.resonator.source: unverified element (catalyst or resonator), modelled as a resonator chamber; ±30 % on its dimensions until inspected

system.elements.muffler.source: shell from owner inspection; internals unknown and modelled as one chamber with two outlets, so its acoustic size is uncertain beyond the shell: ±20 %

system.routes.source: lengths and diameters from forum measurements and owner inspection; ±5 % until measured with a tape (within 1 %)
